data.summary: The code-server directory contains a single Dockerfile that builds a container image running code-server (VS Code in the browser) on top of the shared sandbox-base image. It is a pure infrastructure/deployment artifact of the sandbox environment rather than a business-logic module, and it must be built from the repository root context alongside the other service images. Its role is to expose a browser-accessible IDE inside the sandbox, but it holds no application code, APIs, or data-layer logic of its own.

file_insights.name: Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Dockerfile that layers code-server (browser-based VS Code) onto the shared sandbox-base image, installing it via npm because code-server.dev is blocked in the sandbox network.
file_insights.source_summary: The file starts with `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` and a comment block explaining that this is the Phase D code-server (VS Code in the browser) image. It documents the base image, build context conventions, and the rationale for installing code-server via npm instead of code-server.dev due to network restrictions; the remaining content is the Dockerfile instructions that layer code-server onto the base image.
file_insights.detailed_description: This Dockerfile defines a Phase D sandbox image derived from the shared `sandbox-base` image (built with `make build-base`), which already provides node, python, git, opencode, root user, and WORKDIR /root. The file only adds code-server on top, using an npm-based install path because the upstream code-server.dev distribution endpoint is unreachable from this sandbox's network. Build context is the repository root, matching how docker-compose declares `context: .` and `dockerfile: code-server/Dockerfile` for the `app` service, so the image is part of a multi-service deployment topology rather than a standalone artifact.
responsibilities: Derive the code-server image from the shared sandbox-base image
Install code-server via npm due to blocked upstream distribution endpoint
Align with docker-compose build context (repo root, code-server/Dockerfile) used by the app service
Preserve the base image's root user and /root working directory for sandbox consistency
